stories.summary: Cat A premiums fell 6.4% from the record S$139,001 in the 18 November bidding exercise to S$130,100. Four of the five COE categories fell, with only the Open category up S$2.
stories.title: Cat A COE falls S$8,901 to S$130,100, still S$4,500 more than Cat B
stories.why: COE is the biggest single cost in buying a car in Singapore, and the drop from the record high matters for anyone buying or renewing.

stories.summary: Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow launched SBS Transit's new Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Hub at Sengkang Depot on 18 November. The operator is investing more than S$8 million, and faulty point machines that used to take six months to fix overseas can now be repaired locally in days.
stories.title: SBS Transit opens repair hub that could cut some rail parts' repair time from six months to days
stories.why: Faster local repairs mean less downtime risk for the rail network Singapore relies on every day.

stories.summary: Singapore is advancing international carbon-market cooperation at COP31, including agreements with five countries and a signing with Zambia, to help meet its emissions targets and build a carbon services and trading hub.
stories.title: Singapore steps up international carbon market push to meet emissions targets and create economic value: experts
stories.why: Carbon credits are becoming a real lever for Singapore's climate targets and a new services business.

stories.summary: Singapore must build fusion research expertise before the technology becomes commercially viable or risk falling behind, with NTU's partnership with France's CEA giving students access to French facilities.
stories.title: Singapore told to seek head start in race for fusion power
stories.why: Fusion is a long-horizon energy bet, and Singapore is deciding now whether to build the expertise.

stories.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, $5 above the top of its range, valuing the Claude developer at about $1.5 trillion. Shares begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT today.
stories.title: Anthropic shares list today after pricing IPO at $83, above the $70–$78 range
stories.why: The biggest AI listing of the year is a live test of whether the AI boom still commands premium valuations after a volatile week.

stories.summary: Nvidia fell 2.9% on Wednesday to $150.96, its fifth straight decline, even after reporting third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year on year. The House Energy and Commerce Committee has demanded a briefing by 2 December over alleged export-control violations.
stories.title: Nvidia shares fall for fifth day as House seeks briefing
stories.why: The world's most-watched AI stock is sliding despite a beat-and-raise quarter, and Washington scrutiny is now part of the story.

stories.summary: Nvidia's board recruitment firm, Heidrick & Struggles, has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as part of the search for a successor to Jensen Huang, who resigned last week, and has begun reaching out to candidates.
stories.title: Arm CEO Rene Haas approached for Nvidia top job by board's recruiters
stories.why: The succession question is now driving Nvidia's story as much as its earnings.

stories.summary: UOB is exploring a multilingual call-intelligence tool built on A*STAR's MERaLiON AI model, covering 11 ASEAN languages, to help relationship managers advise clients across Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam, under a signed MOU with A*STAR.
stories.title: UOB explores A*STAR MERaLiON AI call tool for 11 ASEAN languages
stories.why: A Singapore-built multilingual AI model is moving into real banking use.

stories.summary: The Dow fell 561 points, or 1.11%, to 50,198.17, the S&P 500 slipped 0.23% to 7,323.64 and the Nasdaq gained 0.42% after Nvidia's results and the release of hawkish Fed minutes.
stories.title: Wall Street ends mixed after Nvidia earnings, Fed minutes
stories.why: The split close shows markets torn between strong AI earnings and a Fed leaning toward more hikes.

stories.summary: Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed the vast majority of officials see upside inflation risks, with some saying a December hike of more than 25bp could be needed. Governor Waller said a 50bp December hike was possible, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high while oil and gold fell sharply.
stories.title: Fed minutes strike hawkish tone; crude oil and precious metals prices drop sharply
stories.why: Rate-hike expectations are back, and they are moving the dollar, oil and gold at once.

stories.summary: Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen on Thursday for trade talks on tariffs, rare earths and chip export controls, followed by a trilateral session with Putin on Ukraine, arms control and Iran. Expectations for concrete agreements are low.
stories.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen: a triple test for Korean stocks and global markets
stories.why: Three leaders in one room puts tariffs, chips and Ukraine on the same day's agenda.

stories.summary: Australian shares opened sharply lower on Thursday, with the S&P/ASX 200 down 0.9% to 8,745.5, hit by tumbling commodity prices — copper down 5.45% — and Wall Street volatility.
stories.title: ASX suffers sharp dip amid global market headwinds
stories.why: The commodity rout is spilling into Asia-Pacific markets this morning.

stories.summary: France confirmed it periodically sends military personnel into Ukraine to train and maintain supplied weapons, including Mirage 2000-5 jets and Caesar howitzers. Foreign Minister Lavrov called it direct participation in the war, while France says the teams are noncombatants far from the front line.
stories.title: France military personnel in Ukraine for training and maintenance draws Russia response
stories.why: A NATO member's boots on the ground in Ukraine, even in a support role, is a new escalation marker.

stories.summary: PNG and Australia have agreed the Pukpuk Treaty, a new defence pact that lifts their relationship to a formal alliance, with mutual assistance in the event of an armed attack and PNG citizens able to join the Australian Defence Force.
stories.title: Papua New Guinea and Australia agree on historic defence pact
stories.why: A formal Australia–PNG alliance reshapes security in the South Pacific, on Australia's doorstep.

stories.summary: US prosecutors charged Russian national Igor Diu with stalking staff at a Silicon Valley technology and defence firm, alleging he photographed laptop screens, collected home addresses and followed staff to gather intelligence linked to weapons supplied to Ukraine, using Telegram contacts for tasking.
stories.title: Russian national charged in US over stalking Silicon Valley defence firm employees
stories.why: It shows Russian intelligence collection targeting the US defence supply chain directly.

stories.summary: Indra told Reuters it has not been notified of any investigation after El Independiente reported Spain's anti-corruption prosecutor opened a preliminary probe alleging Indra and EM&E were repeatedly favoured in defence contracts, including the 8x8 Dragon armoured vehicle programme.
stories.title: Spanish defence firm Indra says not notified of reported anti-corruption probe
stories.why: A probe into how Spain awards defence contracts could reach one of its biggest suppliers.

stories.summary: King Mohammed VI approved a roadmap for Morocco's defence industry aiming to create about 50,000 direct and indirect jobs by 2035 and meet about 40% of the armed forces' equipment needs, with a strategic agency, an industrial holding company and new zones at Benguerir and Benslimane.
stories.title: Morocco defence industry roadmap targets 50,000 jobs by 2035
stories.why: Morocco is joining the group of countries building a domestic defence industry rather than buying everything abroad.

stories.summary: Russia denied allegations that state-backed hackers targeted a Romanian government institution to intercept NATO and EU emails, while separate ESET research described a purpose-built Exchange tool, 'Cereal', configured to spot messages involving NATO and EU addresses and attributed to the Russia-aligned Turla group with high confidence.
stories.title: Russia rejects Romanian email espionage accusations as Exchange surveillance claims add technical weight
stories.why: Email interception targeting NATO correspondence is a live espionage front — though the scope, and whether any messages were collected, remain unconfirmed.

stories.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines is deploying shore-based anti-ship missiles to Bolinao, Pangasinan, for joint maritime strike exercises in the 10th iteration of AJEX Dagit-PA, which runs 17–27 November and tests planning across land, sea, air, cyber and information warfare capabilities.
stories.title: Anti-ship missiles deployed in Bolinao
stories.why: The exercise explicitly rehearses information warfare alongside missiles in the South China Sea theatre.

stories.summary: RSIS' Benjamin Ang writes that recent hacks — LED screens in Malaysia, supermarket fridges across Europe, and a suspected hack of Ukraine's emergency alert app broadcasting fake nuclear warnings — show how cyberattacks and information campaigns can combine into hybrid attacks that cause panic.
stories.title: Commentary: Cyberattacks on billboards, supermarket fridges reveal a new test of resilience
stories.why: It frames the exact hybrid threat — hacked systems plus rumours — that Singapore's own resilience planning has to cover.

tldr: Singapore: COE Cat A falls S$8,901 from its record high to S$130,100.
Technology: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq today after pricing its IPO at $83, above its range.
Finance: Global stocks slip and the dollar hits a 19-month high as Fed minutes turn hawkish.
Defence: France confirms military personnel in Ukraine; Russia calls it direct participation.
Information warfare: Russia denies Romanian email-espionage claims as researchers link a Turla tool to NATO email interception.
